definition: A self-organizing map (SOM) or self-organizing feature map (SOFM) is an unsupervised machine learning technique used to produce a low-dimensional (typically two-dimensional) representation of a higher-dimensional data set while preserving the topological structure of the data.
details: For example, a data set with p {\displaystyle p} variables measured in n {\displaystyle n} observations could be represented as clusters of observations with similar values for the variables. These clusters then could be visualized as a two-dimensional "map" such that observations in proximal clusters have more similar values than observations in distal clusters. This can make high-dimensional data easier to visualize and analyze. A SOM is a type of artificial neural network but is trained using competitive learning rather than the error-correction learning (e.g., backpropagation with gradient descent) used by other artificial neural networks. The SOM was introduced by the Finnish professor Teuvo Kohonen in the 1980s and therefore is sometimes called a Kohonen map or Kohonen network. The Kohonen map or network is a computationally convenient abstraction building on biological models of neural systems from the 1970s and morphogenesis models dating back to Alan Turing in the 1950s. explainer.lead: A self-organizing map reduces a high-dimensional dataset to a low-dimensional, usually two-dimensional, representation while preserving the topological structure of the data. It matters because it makes high-dimensional data easier to visualize and analyze.

tiers.eli5: It arranges data points on a flat map so that similar things land close together and different things land far apart.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to cluster observations and visualize them as a two-dimensional map where nearby clusters hold more similar values. A pitfall is that the map is a type of neural network trained without supervision, so the layout reflects topology rather than labeled targets.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, for p variables measured in n observations, clusters of observations with similar values are visualized as a two-dimensional map such that observations in proximal clusters are more similar than those in distal clusters. It is a type of artificial neural network trained without supervision.

explainer.example: A dataset with many measured variables across observations is plotted as a 2D map, with similar observations grouped into nearby clusters for inspection.
